brief: A week where a hot flash PMI and jobless claims near multi-year lows gave six Fed officials cover to reiterate more hikes may be needed, pushing October rate-hike odds to 70% and 2027 pricing to 52bps. That drove a global sovereign bond selloff: the 10Y hit its highest since 2007, the 5Y broke above 5% for the first time in nearly two decades, and 30-year mortgage rates topped 7%. The yield surge spilled into credit: Oracle filed a force-majeure notice on its New Mexico data center and its credit risk hit a record high, though Oracle and its partner said the notice does not itself change delivery or financial commitments. Iran-US diplomacy over the Strait of Hormuz produced no resolution; crude eased on the week but retail diesel hit a record high, which BofA says keeps inflation risk elevated even as headline crude falls. Equity gains stayed narrow: Meta's Muse-driven rally added $220bn in market cap while the S&P ex-AI fell about 1% and NYSE new lows outnumbered new highs for a ninth straight day. The dollar rallied and gold fell; bitcoin instead rallied. The note argues rallies should be rented, not owned, until Hormuz reopens, data cools, or auctions clear without tails.
